reproach verb

throw in someone’s teeth

also throw in someone’s face, cast in someone’s teeth, rub it in, hold against, upbraid

classical

Plaut. Most. 300b: Cūr exprobrās?
Cic. Lael. 71: odiōsum sānē genus hominum officia exprobrantium (Lewis & Short)

exprobrō, exprobrāre, exprobrāvī, exprobrātum

verb, first conjugation: aliquid alicui

bring up as a reproach: a fault, or a favour one has done

From probrum.

Examples

  • trīgintā minās prō capite tuō dedī. — Cūr exprobrās?

    I paid thirty minae for your freedom. — Why throw that in my face?Plaut. Most. 300–300b

See also blame, tell off, abuse.

SourcesLewis & Short: exprobro

Plautus, Mostellaria 300–300b.
